scope.summary: Implement multi-actor pose assets per Section 13.18 (BK-18.3, TAI-BK-065), closing AREQ-002/013: MultiActorPoseAsset aligns 2+ bodies by relative root transforms against a shared stage anchor (floor-plane origin, forward +Y stage space), so couple and group sex poses — cowgirl, doggy, missionary, threesome spit-roast arrangements — are placeable as ONE asset; applying re-solves each actor slot in its own body's morph context while preserving relative alignment and declared contact constraints.
acceptance_criteria: MultiActorPoseAsset registers hsk.tailor.multi_actor_pose_asset@1 and stores actors (each a canonical BodyPoseAsset ref plus root transform) against a complete stage frame declaring right-handedness, up/forward axes, linear/angular units, origin/floor policy, rest-pose convention, and an explicit separation between world/stage frame and MT-713 camera extrinsics.

apply_multi_actor(assignments: Vec<(actor_slot, body_id)>) re-solves each slot in its own body's morph context (MT-520 lane) while preserving the relative root alignment; a two-body doggy fixture applied to (neutral, neutral) and to (petite+extreme-breasts, muscular-male) keeps the declared pelvis-to-pelvis relative transform within tolerance in both castings.

Declared contacts consume constraints by hash/reference from canonical hsk.tailor.body_pose_contact_set@1; no local ContactConstraint type exists, and violated canonical constraints report typed findings instead of silently drifting.
Actor slots are assignable to any body whose skeleton version matches; mismatches are typed rejections; slots may not share a body id.
Stage-anchor math: re-rooting the whole asset (move/rotate on the stage) transforms all actors rigidly with contacts intact.
Consumes hsk.tailor.body_pose_contact_set@1 from MT-714 as the sole pin/contact authority and does not introduce a parallel contact record.

Stage, actor-root, body-local, effector, prop, cloth, and camera frame conversions are explicit and unit-tested; re-rooting changes only the declared stage transform and preserves contact-set frame references.
The immutable multi-actor asset hashes its schema/version/revision, stage-frame law, ordered actor/body/BodyPose refs, contact-set ref, and source lineage under the MT-520 canonical hash convention.
scope.risk_if_missed: Couple/group poses stored per-body with no relative alignment must be re-staged by hand every casting change — the production-killing Daz workflow for multi-actor sex scenes; without contact-preserving re-solve, swapping an actor breaks every penetration/contact alignment in the scene.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit skeleton and rigging

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
